x: In a recent article in the Sunday Express, the writer expressed confidence that Britain's young athletes will soon be amongst the world's best. Amongst those mentioned, we were favoured by the mention of seven members:—Broadbent, Clay, Frost, Brown, Marchant, Burfitt and Main.
Throwing the Javelin (Juniors): 1 Dunn (B.), 167 ft. 6½ ins.; 2 Garrett (B.), 134 ft. 6 ins.; 3 Fowler (D.), 119 ft. 5 ins. Senior Relay (1 mile medley): 1 Belgrave (Marchant, Clay, Watts, Hayes).
440 yards (second race): 1 Watson (G.); 2 Ewart (T.); 3 Strutt (R.); 4 Caers (B. & P.). 54.3 secs. 880 yards: 1 Marchant (B.); 2 Watson (G.); 4 Edwards (B.).

We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson.

Ted Stimpson was always well up with the first dozen runners, but Vern Blowfield was suffering with shoe trouble and was gradually dropping back while Len Herbert and Marchant were striving to hold their places, but things did not look too good for our prospects of retaining our title as Southern champions.

Those who were fortunate enough to get in front of the field over the first mile stayed there, and during the whole race the leading men remained the same, Frank Abberton, Bowering (S.L.H.) and Barry (H.H.H.) fighting for first place, Bill Lucas and Marchant being a few places further back.

Len Marchant set a fast pace from the start and quickly gained a 30 yds. lead, which was not lost until the beginning of the second lap when Bill Lucas with Gorton and Palmer, of Cambridge, in close attendance, took up the running.
In the mile Marchant qualified in 4.31 and Burfitt in 4 mins 33 secs. In the final Burfitt was fourth and Marchant sixth.
Bishop (winner's time, 1 min. 57.8 secs.) 1 mile: 1st, Marchant; 2nd, Bromley. 4 min. 26 secs. 2 miles: 1st, Blowfield, 9 min. 41 secs.; 2nd.
Marchant and John Brown also competed. Charlie Smart made a gallant effort in the 6 miles on Friday evning and eventually finished fifth in 30 min. 42 secs., thus gaining a standard medal.
100 yards: 1st, Lowers, 10.5 secs. 220 yards: 1st, Sexton, 23.4 secs. 440 yards: 1st, Cope, 53.6 secs.; 3rd, Underwood. 880 yards: 1st, Marchant 1 min. 59.5 secs.; 3rd, A.
"A Southern Counties 6-Stage Relay was held from Belgrave Hall on April 4th over a four and three-quarter miles lap. Belgrave were winners with Marchant, Patience, Shields, Penny, Cohen and Carter.
